classification.difficultyReason: Sum the required lengths, divide by the stock length and round up for purchasing, then charge for the full purchased length rather than the required length and round the cost.

content.prompt: Inouk wanted to edge her garden beds with timber. She measured the lengths of the edges as 1.48 metres, 9.2 metres, 0.93 metres, 4.02 metres and 5.45 metres. How many 4.2-metre lengths of timber garden edging did she have to buy? If the timber garden edging costs $\$3.44$ per metre, how much did Inouk’s garden edging project cost her? Give the cost to the nearest cent.

answer.short:
6 lengths; $\$86.69$.

Round the number of lengths up, then calculate the cost of all the timber purchased.
answer.worked:
The total length needed is
$$\begin{align*}1.48+9.2+0.93+4.02+5.45&=21.08\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The number of 4.2-metre lengths needed is
$$\begin{align*}21.08\div4.2&=210.8\div42\\21.08\div4.2&=5\frac{2}{105}.\end{align*}$$
Five lengths provide only $5\times4.2=21$ m, so she must buy 6 lengths.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Length purchased}&=6\times4.2\\\text{Length purchased}&=25.2\text{ m}\\\text{Cost}&=25.2\times\$3.44\\\text{Cost}&=\$86.688\\\text{Cost}&\approx\$86.69.\end{align*}$$
